extra.message: Privilege escalation via self-assigned role at registration — Attacker gains school_admin privileges at account creation, obtaining unrestricted access to all student PII, grades, audit logs, user management, course administration, and CSV import/export functions. [verified: Identical vulnerability to [0]: the role field in SignUpForm (forms.py:16) and unchecked form.save() in signup (views.py:89) permit any anonymous user to register with school_admin privileges.]

Path Traversal in course_spool_slot_094 — unvalidated filename on file upload — Arbitrary file write to any location on the filesystem; overwrite of application code, static assets, or system files; potential code execution via cron job or script planting. [verified: course_spool_slot_094 passes the client-supplied filename (drop_blob.name) directly to FileSystemStorage.save() with no path sanitization; _wrk_gate provides auth only, enabling arbitrary file writes by token holders.]

Insecure Deserialization via pickle.loads in course_bundle_thaw_185 — Remote code execution via crafted pickle payload; full server compromise, data theft, lateral movement. [verified: course_bundle_thaw_185 calls pickle.loads() on raw request body or 'blob' GET param (optionally b64-decoded) with zero integrity validation; _wrk_gate authenticates but does not neutralize deserialization of attacker-crafted payloads.]

Path Traversal in course_vault_stash_250 — arbitrary file write with sensitive data — Arbitrary file write to any location reachable by the Django process; overwrite of application code, templates, or configuration to achieve code execution; exposure of SSN and credit card data written to attacker-chosen paths. [verified: course_vault_stash_250 constructs target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json' with the unsanitized 'ref' GET param, allowing traversal (e.g. ../../etc/cron.d); _wrk_gate provides auth only, no path sanitization or restriction.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 in course_jinja_cast_683 — Remote code execution on the server; full compromise of the LMS, database access, environment variable theft including INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN and SECRET_KEY. [verified: course_jinja_cast_683 concatenates the unsanitized GET param 'fragment' into a Jinja2 Template string rendered as text/html; only the _wrk_gate shared-secret check intervenes, which authenticates but does not validate or escape input, enabling SSTI→RCE by any token holder.]

OS Command Injection via os.system in course_shell_probe_701 — Arbitrary command execution on the server; ability to read/write filesystem, exfiltrate database credentials and secrets, pivot to internal network. [verified: course_shell_probe_701 passes the unsanitized 'host' GET param directly to os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) with no shell escaping; _wrk_gate provides auth only, leaving arbitrary command execution possible for any token holder.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY — Session forgery, CSRF bypass, password reset token forgery, and signature tampering for any Django feature relying on SECRET_KEY. [verified: Same hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY at settings.py line 8-9; if deployed without the environment variable, an attacker with repository access can forge sessions and signed tokens.]

Hardcoded Default Django SECRET_KEY Fallback — If deployed without setting the SECRET_KEY environment variable, an attacker who knows the repository's default key can forge authenticated sessions for any user, bypass CSRF protection, and decrypt signed tokens including password reset links, achieving full account takeover. [verified: settings.py line 9 provides a hardcoded fallback 'django-insecure-local-dev-only' when SECRET_KEY env var is unset; this known key enables session forgery, CSRF bypass, and password-reset token forgery.]

CSRF via GET on state-changing endpoints (admin_user_toggle and 4 others) — Attacker can trick an authenticated school_admin into disabling arbitrary user accounts, or an instructor into changing assignment statuses / releasing grades / locking discussion threads, all without a valid CSRF token, by having the victim visit a crafted link or page. [verified: admin_user_toggle (line 598), assignment_status (line 347), release_grade (line 419), request_resubmission (line 442), and discussion_moderate (line 545) all mutate database state without @require_POST or any HTTP-method guard; Django's CsrfViewMiddleware exempts GET requests from CSRF token validation, so a crafted or tag pointing to these URLs triggers state changes with no CSRF p]

IDOR — Teaching Assistant can export grades for any cohort — A teaching assistant can download a CSV containing grades, feedback, and release status for all students in any cohort — horizontal privilege escalation across the entire LMS — by simply varying the cohort_pk URL parameter. [verified: export_grades checks cohort.instructors membership for instructor-role users (line 782) but performs zero cohort-scoped check for teaching_assistant users; the role gate at line 784 passes TAs unconditionally, so a TA assigned to any single cohort can enumerate cohort_pk (sequential integer) and download full grade reports including PII, feedback, and release status from every cohort in the system]

IDOR — any authenticated user can download files with null course association — Unauthorized access to all user-uploaded files (assignments, documents, datasets) uploaded via the file_upload endpoint, regardless of ownership. [verified: file_upload at line 843 creates Resource objects without setting the course field (model defaults to null=True), and file_download at line 860 skips all authorization checks when resource.course is None for any user who is not the uploader and not a school_admin; any authenticated user can download another user's uploaded files by guessing sequential resource primary keys.]

Missing authorization on file downloads — course-less resources accessible to all authenticated users and TA bypass — Any authenticated user can download files uploaded by other users through the normal file upload flow (IDOR via sequential IDs). Teaching assistants can download any course-associated resource regardless of cohort assignment. This exposes potentially sensitive documents submitted as course resources. [verified: Same authorization gaps as findings 2 and 6: file_download line 861-863 checks student enrollment and instructor cohort membership but omits any check for teaching_assistant role, allowing TAs to download any course-associated resource; when resource.course is None (the norm for file_upload-created resources, line 843), the inner authorization block is skipped and any authenticated non-uploader/no]

NoSQL Injection via raw MongoDB filter in course_mongo_lane_711 — Unauthorized data access to all MongoDB collections; potential server-side JavaScript execution on MongoDB; data exfiltration or corruption of the ops.records collection. [verified: course_mongo_lane_711 passes the unsanitized 'filter' key (or entire JSON body) directly to MongoDB find_one(); _wrk_gate provides only auth with no query sanitization, enabling NoSQL operator injection by token holders.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in course_xml_fold_735 — Arbitrary local file read including secrets and source code; internal SSRF via entity resolution; denial of service via XML entity expansion. [verified: course_xml_fold_735 parses the raw request body with an lxml parser configured load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False; _wrk_gate is only auth, leaving XXE-based file read and SSRF exploitable by token holders.]

Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints — Unlimited brute-force attacks against login, signup, and password-reset endpoints, enabling credential guessing and account takeover. [verified: No rate-limiting middleware, decorator, or third-party package exists anywhere in settings.py, urls.py, views.py, or requirements.txt; login, signup, and password-reset endpoints are publicly reachable with zero brute-force protection.]

Account enumeration via signup username uniqueness error — Attacker can enumerate valid usernames to mount targeted password guessing, credential stuffing, or phishing attacks. [verified: SignUpForm extends Django UserCreationForm which performs username uniqueness validation and returns the distinct error 'A user with that username already exists.' on duplicates; rendered in signup.html via field.errors.0 with no rate limiting, enabling username enumeration.]

Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints — Attackers can brute-force credentials via the login endpoint, enumerate valid usernames via the signup endpoint (duplicate username error), or spam account creation to exhaust resources (DoS). [verified: No rate-limiting mechanism exists anywhere: django-ratelimit is absent from INSTALLED_APPS, no custom throttling middleware is registered, no @ratelimit or throttling decorators appear on login/signup/password-reset views, and no hand-rolled rate-limiting logic is present in any view or utility; login, signup, and password-reset endpoints are fully exposed to brute-force and enumeration attacks.]

Discussion Views Missing Course-Scope Authorization for Instructors/TAs — An instructor or TA assigned to one course can view, create, and comment on discussion threads in any other course, potentially accessing private course discussions or disrupting other courses' forums. [verified: discussion_create (line 492) and discussion_detail (line 514) gate access with 'request.user.is_instructor() or request.user.is_teaching_assistant()' without checking whether the instructor/TA belongs to any cohort of the target course; contrast with discussion_moderate (line 547) which DOES check thread.course.cohorts.filter(instructors=request.user), confirming the course-scope check was intenti]

CSRF via GET on discussion_moderate — state-changing endpoint without CSRF protection — Cross-site request forgery allowing an attacker to lock, hide, pin, or reopen discussion threads on behalf of an authenticated instructor/TA/admin; disruption of course discussions. [verified: discussion_moderate performs state changes (thread.status=action, thread.save()) on unguarded GET requests. Django's CsrfViewMiddleware deliberately exempts GET from CSRF checks, and the template uses plain <a href> links without CSRF tokens, so any authenticated moderator clicking a crafted link silently alters thread status.]

CSV formula injection in grade and submission exports — Arbitrary command execution on the machine of the administrator or instructor who opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application. [verified: Same CSV formula injection as findings 0, 1, and 7: csv.writer at export_grades line 794 and export_submissions_report line 818 receives user-influenced display_name, assignment.title, and feedback text; no form validation, middleware, or output sanitization strips formula-triggering =, +, -, @ prefixes from any of these fields before CSV emission.]

CSV formula injection in export_submissions_report — Same as export_grades—formula execution in spreadsheet applications when the exported CSV is opened, affecting the school-admin-only submissions report. [verified: export_submissions_report writes course.title, cohort.name, assignment.title, and student.display_name() to CSV without formula sanitization; all four fields are user-controlled through CourseForm, CohortForm, AssignmentForm, and SignUpForm respectively, none of which validate or strip formula-triggering prefix characters.]

Open Redirect via unvalidated redirect target in course_return_lane_163 — Phishing and social engineering attacks leveraging the trusted LMS domain; potential to steal INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN via referer leakage or credential harvesting. [verified: course_return_lane_163 passes the unsanitized 'lane' GET/POST param directly to Django's redirect(); _wrk_gate provides auth only with no URL validation, enabling open-redirect phishing by token holders.]

Missing authorization on public operations endpoint course_grade_file_096 — Unauthenticated access to internal operational metrics and business-sensitive memos that should be restricted behind the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN gate. [verified: Same as [10] — course_grade_file_096 lacks _wrk_gate, exposing internal operational data without authentication.]

Sensitive PII Stored in Plaintext on Disk in course_vault_stash_250 — Exposure of SSN-like and credit-card-like data in plaintext JSON files; compliance violation; data usable for identity theft if real values are stored. [verified: course_vault_stash_250 writes SSN-like and credit-card-like values from GET params to a plaintext JSON file on disk with no encryption-at-rest; _wrk_gate controls access to the write endpoint but does not protect the data at rest.]

Account enumeration via signup form username validation — Attacker can enumerate valid usernames for targeted password attacks, credential stuffing, or social engineering. [verified: SignUpForm extends Django's UserCreationForm which performs uniqueness validation on the username field and returns field-level errors (e.g., 'A user with that username already exists') with no generic error override; combined with the total absence of rate limiting (finding 3), an attacker can systematically probe usernames to enumerate valid accounts.]

Permissive CORS — origin reflection with credentials enabled — Cross-origin data theft from any origin when combined with other ops endpoints, enabling an attacker to exfiltrate data from authenticated internal callers. [verified: Same CORS misconfiguration as [7] in course_origin_mirror_661; low impact because auth uses header token, not cookies.]

Missing authentication gate on course_identity_ping_344 ops endpoint — Unauthenticated access to an internal operations endpoint—bypasses the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN gate that protects all other ops/ routes. Enables information probing and could be combined with other vulnerabilities. [verified: course_identity_ping_344 has NO _wrk_gate check (line 102-104), making it reachable without any authentication; it only echoes user-supplied handle/channel back as JSON with no sensitive data exposure.]

Security Headers Disabled — X-XSS-Protection and CSP blanked in course_frame_slip_671 — Weakened browser security posture for any content served from this endpoint; facilitiates XSS exploitation if combined with other injection vulnerabilities. [verified: course_frame_slip_671 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection:0 and CSP:'' on its response; _wrk_gate controls who can reach the endpoint but the security-weakening headers are served to any authenticated caller, reducing browser defenses.]

CORS misconfiguration with credential reflection in course_origin_mirror_661 — An attacker can host a malicious page that makes authenticated cross-origin requests to the LMS, reading sensitive data or performing actions as the victim user. [verified: course_origin_mirror_661 reflects the Origin header with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true on a reachable path (behind _wrk_gate), but auth uses a custom header token not cookies, severely limiting practical CORS impact.]

Information Disclosure — DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE exposed in course_trace_panel_742 — Reveals internal Django configuration module name to attackers, aiding reconnaissance and targeted attacks against the application framework. [verified: course_trace_panel_742 returns DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE env var in its JSON response; _wrk_gate prevents unauthenticated access but the information disclosure aids reconnaissance for any token holder.]
